newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dachser says Spain airbridge saved Opel millions.
newsitem.headline: Dachser says Spain airbridge saved Opel millions.

text.p: German forwarder Dachser GmbH & Co said it saved Adam Opel AG several million marks in lost production by flying in car parts from Spain during the Spanish truckers' strike which ended last week.

Opel was able to keep production rolling at its Eisenach plant for a vital few extra days after Dachser, fellow forwarder Sostmeier and Spanish partner Cotransa set up an emergency airbridge, a Dachser statement said.
The parts in question were seat components without which production could not have continued.
Opel first stopped production of its Corsa model at Eisenach on Thursday but was able to resume work normally on Friday.
Dachser chartered helicopters to fly over the heads of striking truckers into Opel's strike-hit parts factory in Vitoria, Spain, and carry parts to Vitoria airport.
Eight tonnes of parts were flown out of the factory and a further ten tonnes were diverted from a truck already travelling in Spain, Dachser said.
A chartered Antonov-12 aircraft then flew the freight on late-night flights on Tuesday and Wednesday to Erfurt airport from where it was trucked to the Eisenach plant.
Dachser, one of Germany's largest family-owned freight forwarders, said the airbridge was organised in co-operation with Osnabrueck-based forwarder Sostmeier and its Spain partner Cotransa.
